classification.difficultyReason: Derive a missing cross-section side by Pythagoras then combine two ends with perimeter-times-depth, alongside ordinary volume. Shape and methods are familiar, no proof or new model invented.

content.prompt: For each solid calculate (i) the surface area and (ii) the volume. Give exact answers and, where needed, also an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Right-trapezium prism, front parallel bases14/5cm perpendicularheight6cm, extrusion8cm. Original physical rightangle relationships retained.
spec.mathematics: Explicit closed prism physical front/depth/view model, every hiddenedge derived by native geometry. Right-angle marks use projected physical perpendicular pairs. All original dimensions; no derived length shown.

answer.worked:
The trapezium cross-section has area 57 cm². Its sloping side is $\sqrt{(14-5)^2+6^2}=3\sqrt{13}\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{end}}&=\frac12(14+5)6=57\\S&=2(57)+8(14+5+6+3\sqrt{13})\\S&=(314+24\sqrt{13})\text{ cm}^2\\S&\approx400.53\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

The third side of the right triangle is $\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{aligned}S&=2(\tfrac12(12)(5))+20(12+5+13)\\S&=60+600=660\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
